findings.title: Interpreter exit overtakes a producer deleter already running on another thread
findings.scenario: A daemon thread calls the add-on with a versioned read-only output. The Operand constructor consumes it, refuses the write, and runs its producer deleter during unwinding. That finite callback sleeps with the GIL released. Main-thread atexit synchronize sees zero queued entries and returns; CPython finalizes before the callback finishes, forcing an unwind through the catch-all/noexcept boundary and aborting. The same gap exists in deferred release after popping a completed entry.
findings.evidence: Fresh unchanged full add-on: addon_exit_full_cpu.py aborts rc134 under timeout15, FATAL: exception not rethrown; --control joins the worker and exits0. No CUDA launch/event acquisition is reachable before the read-only refusal. Actual-source deferred trace independently aborts child rc-6 after CALLBACK IN PROGRESS entries=0 and HOOK returned entries=0. CUDA-call replacements only in the deferred trace.
findings.fix: Track admitted add-on releases independently of the pending queue; close admission in atexit and wait with the GIL released for all other-thread admitted callbacks to leave before finalization. Leak later releases without entering Python, use self-exclusion, and contain ordinary C++ exceptions only. Apply this to immediate, deferred and capsule callback release paths.
findings.prior_art: CPython 3.12 lifecycle/GIL (PSF, 2023); C++17 noexcept; standard admission/quiescence pattern as core ImportReleaseLifecycle. Taken: contracts and existing guard pattern; ours: add-on queue-hidden callback witness.
findings.introduced: Initial add-on lifecycle, not FIX4; N5/V3-01 originally core-only.

findings.title: A recoverable event-query error is consumed without being reported or remembered
findings.scenario: cudaEventQuery in drain_completed returns a one-time error, then later stream synchronization and event query succeed. drain_completed clears the slot but records no error; the next synchronize silently succeeds.
findings.evidence: CPU actual-source trace query_error_cpu.py: slot 0; release_errors and unreported_release_errors 0; next synchronize success, manager deleted once. Interposer GPU probe pending.
findings.fix: Persist non-NotReady query failures before consuming the slot, and report them once at synchronize while continuing safe completion/release logic.
findings.prior_art: NVIDIA CUDA 12.6 event-query return-code and last-error contracts (2024). Taken: checked returns and consume-after-accounting; ours: one-shot query-failure scenario.
findings.introduced: FIX4 consumes the query error without preserving it.

findings.title: A successfully created cuBLAS handle leaks when the host cache insertion fails
findings.scenario: All handle settings succeed, then handles.emplace(device,h) throws std::bad_alloc. The raw handle has no owner/catch on this path, never reaches the cache, and is never destroyed. Repeated attempts can leak a handle and its device resources per failed host insertion.
findings.evidence: CPU unchanged-function slices with successful cuBLAS-call replacements and one real operator new failure after the last setting: conv creates=1 destroys=0; lstm creates=1 destroys=0; probe rc1. No CUDA execution.
findings.fix: Keep a newly created handle in scoped ownership through both settings and map insertion; destroy it on every exception before insertion commits, checking cleanup status without throwing during unwinding.
findings.prior_art: ISO C++17 RAII/exception safety (2017), NVIDIA cuBLAS12.6 create/destroy resource contract (2024). Taken: scoped ownership until transfer; ours: cache-insertion OOM witness.
findings.introduced: Initial P1-T cache creation; FIX4 D7 closes setting failures only.

findings.title: The new fill_ narrows a supported int64 element count to a wrapped grid and can silently fill only a prefix
findings.scenario: For n=2**40+1 fp32 elements, the shape/byte bounds fit int64. fill_ calls the baseline nblk helper, which narrows ceil(n/256)=2**32+1 to int1 on the reviewed ABI. The non-grid-stride fill kernel then writes only256 elements, its launch succeeds, and the revision is bumped. This is a huge descriptor boundary (4TiB+4bytes), not a resident array reproduction on the lead GPU.
findings.evidence: CPU exact-helper arithmetic witness: n=1099511627777 grid=1 covered=256; rc1, no UBSan error because signed narrowing is implementation-defined. The defect is the new fill_ call site reusing an insufficient helper; no baseline full/other engine op is classified as newly broken.
findings.fix: Before narrowing in the new fill_ path, calculate the block count in int64 and explicitly refuse counts exceeding the supported grid.x bound. Alternatively use a reviewed capped grid-stride fill path, without silently narrowing; preserving the no-new-core-kernel plan favors the refusal.
findings.prior_art: ISO C++17 integral conversions and NVIDIA CUDA12.6 grid/dim3 semantics. Taken: checked narrowing/launch bounds; ours: int64 fill boundary witness.
findings.introduced: Initial new fill_ binding uses a pre-existing helper without a new size rail.
